title: Fixed Alternating Stack with Thickness Optimization for Dual Stopband
scientific_hypothesis: A 36-layer alternating Ta2O5/SiO2 stack with optimized individual layer thicknesses can simultaneously achieve low transmittance in both 355-365 nm and 1030-1080 nm bands while maintaining high transmittance in 420-700 nm, without requiring material substitution or topology changes.
design_principle: Quarter-wave optical thickness stacks create constructive interference for reflection at the design wavelength. By tuning layer thicknesses away from simple quarter-wave values, the stopband positions and widths can be adjusted. Multiple periods increase stopband depth. From recalled thin-film theory, a high-index/low-index alternating stack produces a primary stopband centered near the quarter-wave condition, with higher-order stopbands at harmonic wavelengths.
proposed_topology: Air | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Fused Silica

minimize average transmittance in 1030-1080 nm band

minimize transmittance at 355 nm single wavelength

theory_basis: Quarter-wave stacks produce stopbands centered at wavelengths where optical thickness equals lambda/4
Alternating high/low index pairs create Bragg reflection conditions
Stopband depth increases with number of periods in a periodic stack
Higher-order stopbands appear at approximately odd harmonics of the fundamental design wavelength
Ta2O5/SiO2 is a standard high-index/low-index pair for visible and near-UV filters from recalled thin-film practice
expected_advantages: Fixed topology reduces search space complexity compared to variable layer count
36 layers provides sufficient periods for deep stopbands if thicknesses are well-optimized
Alternating structure is manufacturable with standard deposition processes
Thickness optimization alone can shift stopband positions without material changes
known_risks: Ta2O5 material name may not resolve in the local registry - if rejected, need to use the exact measurement name the registry provides
Quarter-wave design at 355 nm may not naturally produce strong rejection at 1030-1080 nm without careful thickness tuning
36 layers may be insufficient for deep rejection in both stopbands simultaneously
Thickness bounds (20-350 nm, relaxed to 15-355 nm) may constrain achievable optical thickness combinations
Recalled Ta2O5 refractive index at 355 nm is approximately 2.2-2.3 but actual dataset value may differ
No literature validation of this specific dual-band configuration - performance is uncertain until simulation runs
Previous iterations failed due to target band not overlapping simulation grid - wavelength range must cover 350-1100 nm minimum
execution_request_english: Design a planar multilayer dielectric filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence at 0 degrees under unpolarized illumination. The stack consists of exactly 36 layers in alternating sequence: Ta2O5 (Gao), SiO2 (Gao), Ta2O5 (Gao), SiO2 (Gao), repeating 18 times, terminating on fused silica. Optimize individual layer thicknesses within the range 15-355 nm per layer. The simulation wavelength grid must span 350 nm to 1100 nm with sufficient resolution to evaluate all target bands. Target objectives: minimize average transmittance in 355-365 nm band, minimize average transmittance in 1030-1080 nm band, maximize average transmittance in 420-700 nm band, and minimize transmittance at 355 nm single wavelength. Materials are Ta2O5 (Gao) and SiO2 (Gao) from the catalog. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates count, tightest_margin, run_status, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates.
revision_reason: Previous iterations failed compilation due to target band not overlapping simulation grid. This revision expands wavelength coverage to 350-1100 nm and relaxes thickness bounds to 15-355 nm per feedback directive for zero valid candidates.
